diagnostic_evidence.quote:
According to Lemma \ref{lem4},
for each $\E\left(|s_{\tau_i}|^2|r_{\tau_i}|^2\frac{1}{\|S_{\tau}A_{\tau}\|_2^2}\right)$ in (\ref{lem5Eq1}), it holds that

issues.failure_explanation: Finiteness of the first moments of X and Y does not imply that XY is integrable, so E(XY) may fail to exist while the right-hand side is defined. Counterexample: X >= 0 with E[X] finite but E[X^2] infinite, S an independent Rademacher variable, Y = XS; then E|Y| < infinity and E(Y|X) = 0 a.s., so E[X E(Y|X)] = 0, but E(XY) = E(X^2 S) does not exist. The claimed identity is the tower property, whose standard statement requires E|XY| < infinity (or nonnegativity side conditions); as stated the lemma is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis E|XY| < infinity.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is unreliable as a general statement. Its only application (in the proof of Lemma lem6) uses nonnegative, a.s.-finite quantities, where the identity is valid, so no downstream result is damaged.
issues.title: Lemma lem4 (tower property) stated with an insufficient integrability hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A single missing standard hypothesis; the repair is local, changes nothing in the paper's application, and every substantive claim survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $A\in\reals^{m\times n}$ be a
  nonzero matrix, $r\in\range(A)$ be a nonzero vector, and $S\in\mathbb{DR}^{m\times m}$ be a nonsingular diagonal matrix.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow A to have zero rows (only 'nonzero matrix' is assumed, and condition (marDistribMatrixProperty) in Definition def:batchSampling only constrains the sampling probabilities). If a zero row is drawn with positive probability in a batch whose rows are all zero rows, then ||S_tau A_tau||_2 = 0 on a positive-probability event: the proof step dividing by ||S_tau A_tau||_2^2 is undefined, beta^S_{i,j} = 0 although p_{ij} > 0, B_{S;i} is singular, and B_{S;i}^{-1} (hence D^2 in Theorem convRBSK and all later rate formulas) does not exist. Simplest instance: A = (1,0)^T in R^{2x1}, q = 1, probabilities (1/2,1/2), which satisfies Definition def:batchSampling but gives beta^S_{1,2} = 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis that A has no zero rows (equivalently delete zero rows, harmless for consistent systems since they force b_j = 0); then every batch sampled with positive probability contains a nonzero row and all beta^S_{i,j} with p_{ij} > 0 are positive.
issues.overall_effect: In the admitted degenerate configurations the auxiliary objects B_{S;i}^{-1} and D^2 are undefined and the proof of Lemma lem6 is invalid as written, so the statements of Theorem convRBSK, Corollary convRBSK_relaxed, Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave and Theorem convRBSK_sharper are ill-defined for matrices with zero rows. (With the natural 0/0 convention the final inequalities remain true, so the loss is the missing hypothesis, not the results.)
issues.title: Zero rows of A make beta^S_{i,j} vanish, so B_{S;i}^{-1}, D^2 and the proof of Lemma lem6 are ill-defined
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis repairs the degenerate case; the method, the conclusions, the rates and the advertised scope are all unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let the columns of matrices  $V_{\tau}\in\reals^{n\times d_{\tau}}$ and $W_{\tau}\in\reals^{n\times (d-d_{\tau})}$
  be the orthonormal bases of the subspaces $\range(A_{\tau}^{\T})$ and $\mathcal{W}_{\tau}$, respectively.

Let $\mathcal{W}_{\tau}\subseteq\range(A^{\T})$ be a subspace satisfying the facts
  $\mathcal{W}_{\tau}\perp\range(A_{\tau}^{\T})$ and $\dim(\mathcal{W}_{\tau})=d-d_{\tau}$.

issues.failure_explanation: When a batch tau in the support of P has d_tau = dim range(A_tau^T) = d (possible whenever q >= rank(A), e.g., a batch of d distinct generic rows), the space W_tau is {0}, W_tau is an n-by-0 matrix, and lambda_min(W_tau^T A^T D^2 A W_tau) is the smallest eigenvalue of a 0x0 matrix, which is undefined; hence xi = min_tau xi_tau is undefined for such instances. (For those batches the error is already zero, so the intended content is fine, but no convention is stated.) The same undefined quantity recurs in widehat{xi} of Corollary convRBSK_relaxed, widetilde{xi} of Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave, and xi_{tau^{(k-1)}} / E(xi_tau) of Theorem convRBSK_sharper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the minima over tau to batches with d_tau < d (batches with d_tau = d force the error to zero, so they can be assigned any value in [0,1] or excluded).
issues.overall_effect: The rate constants in Theorem convRBSK and in all three subsequent rate results are ill-defined for admitted instances in which some batch has full row rank; as written the bounds do not cover that regime (e.g., q >= rank(A) with spanning batches in the support).
issues.title: Rate constant xi (and its later variants) is undefined when a sampled batch spans the full row space
issues.why_classification: A local definitional convention fixes the degenerate case; no method, conclusion, rate or scope changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
D^2 &=& S^{\T}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{q} B_{S;i}^{-1} P_i\right)S \\
  &=& S^{\T}\left(B_S^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^{q} P_i\right)S \\
  &\succeq& S^{\T}B_S^{-1} \widehat{P}S.

issues.failure_explanation: In Lemma lem6, ||S_tau A_tau||_2^2 is computed on the q-row batch matrix, so repeated row indices are counted with multiplicity: ||S_tau A_tau||_2^2 = || sum_{j'} n(tau,j') s_{j'}^2 a_{j'} a_{j'}^T || (this reading is forced by the proof identity ||S_tau r_tau||_2^2 = sum_{i=1}^q |s_{tau_i}|^2 |r_{tau_i}|^2). When a paving block T_t has fewer than q rows, every draw with effective set T_t contains repetitions, which generically strictly inflate the spectral norm beyond ||S_{T_t} A_{T_t}||_2^2. The paper's own Example exampRowPaving is a counterexample: the singleton block T_1 = {1} is drawn as tau = (1,1) with probability 1/2, giving beta^S_{i,1} = ||S_{(1,1)} A_{(1,1)}||_2^2 = 2 s_1^2 ||A^{(1)}||_2^2, whereas the proof claims beta^S_{i,1} = ||S_{T_1} A_{T_1}||_2^2 = s_1^2 ||A^{(1)}||_2^2. Hence B_{S;i} = B_S is false; in fact B_{S;i} succeq B_S (multiplicity only adds PSD terms), so B_{S;i}^{-1} preceq B_S^{-1} and the valid relation is D^2 preceq S^T B_S^{-1} P-tilde S, the opposite direction from the inequality D^2 succeq S^T B_S^{-1} Phat S that the proof needs. The claimed gain matrix S^T B_S^{-1} Phat S can strictly exceed the valid D^2 of Theorem convRBSK in some entries, so the bounds (thm3Result)-(thm3Eq4) can be strictly more optimistic than the established bound and are unproven as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave (and the corresponding evaluations in Remarks remark:relaxOne and remark:relaxTwo) to pavings whose blocks all have cardinality q, so no repetitions occur and beta^S_{i,j} = ||S_{T_{I(j)}} A_{T_{I(j)}}||_2^2 genuinely holds; this covers the paper's experiments. Alternatively, restate the theorem with B_S replaced by the true multiplicity-aware quantities, which changes (weakens) the stated bounds. No source-supported argument establishes the stated bounds for general pavings.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave's bounds are unsupported whenever the paving has a block smaller than q (the generic row-paving case the framework advertises, cf. Example exampRowPaving). The same multiplicity-blind norm evaluation makes remark:relaxOne's formula (betaS_value) for Examples exampRowPaving and exampNonUnique false and invalidates the claim that the relaxed bound (rlx_upperBound_1) 'recovers' Needell's RBK bound: for unequal pavings the paper's valid relaxed bound uses the larger multiplicity-aware beta^I and is strictly worse than the printed (rlx_upperBound_1). It also breaks remark:relaxTwo's comparison that Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave's bounds are sharper than Corollary convRBSK_relaxed's and Needell's. The experimental curves labelled 'Thm convRBSK_relaxed_pave bound' use equal-size blocks and are unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave falsely equates beta^S_{i,j} with the effective-set block norm; with padded (repeated) indices the key relaxation D^2 succeq S^T B_S^{-1} Phat S is unsupported
issues.why_classification: A contained repair exists (restrict to equal-cardinality blocks, matching the experiments, or restate with corrected, weaker constants), so no new global proof architecture is required and a recognizably comparable result survives; but the repair either excludes the advertised general unequal-paving regime or changes the stated bound, which is more than a routine local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: Step (thm4Eq5) applies Lemma lem5 to the sequences xi_{tau^{(k-1,j)}} and ||x^{(k,j)} - x_star||_2^2, which requires nonnegative sample covariance of xi with the SQUARED error norm. The theorem's hypothesis only assumes nonnegative sample covariance of xi with the UNSQUARED norm, which does not imply the needed condition: e.g., sequences xi = (0,0,1,1) and y = (0.1, 10, 5.4, 5.6) have sample cov(xi, y) > 0 but sample cov(xi, y^2) < 0. The premise actually used in the proof is therefore not established by the stated hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the covariance condition for the pair (xi_{tau^{(k-1)}}, ||x^{(k)} - x_star||_2^2), as the proof actually uses.
issues.overall_effect: Independently of the later inference failure, the stated sufficient condition of Theorem convRBSK_sharper does not justify step (thm4Eq5); the theorem as stated rests on an unestablished premise.
issues.title: Theorem convRBSK_sharper's covariance hypothesis is on the unsquared error norm, but the proof needs it on the squared norm
issues.why_classification: The forced correction is a single hypothesis change with no effect on the intended rate, scope or method; it is not a pure typo because a premise must be repaired (the unsquared condition is genuinely insufficient), but the fix is local and loss-free.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\E_k^{(j)}\left(\|x^{(k+1,j)}-x_{\star}\|_2^2\right)
	&\leq& \left(1+\epsilon-\E\left(\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}} \right)\right) \left(\frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\|x^{(k,j)}-x_{\star}\|_2^2\right).
\end{eqnarray}
 which holds with probability at least $1-\delta$.

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality (thm4Eq8) is proved only on an event of probability at least 1-delta over the l auxiliary realizations; on the complementary delta-event the relation between the two sides is uncontrolled, and the two sides are dependent random quantities (both are functions of the same sampled batches), so their expectations need not inherit the inequality. Moreover, the left side is a sample average of conditional expectations and the right side involves the sample average of the squared errors, whereas the conclusion (thm4Eq2) contains only deterministic population quantities (E||x^{(k)}-x_star||^2 and E(xi_tau)); consequently the claimed 'with probability at least 1-delta' attaches to a statement with no sample-dependent content, making the quantifier structure ill-posed. Nothing in the proof controls the failure event or justifies identifying the sample averages with the population expectations, so (thm4Eq2) is not established.

failure_location.quote: Taking expectation on both sides of (\ref{thm4Eq8}) leads to the sharper estimate (\ref{thm4Eq2}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem at the population level: from (thm4Eq3), taking full expectation gives E||e^{(k+1)}||^2 <= E||e^{(k)}||^2 - E[xi_{tau^{(k-1)}} ||e^{(k)}||^2], so under the POPULATION condition Cov(xi_{tau^{(k-1)}}, ||x^{(k)}-x_star||_2^2) >= 0 the deterministic bound E||e^{(k+1)}||^2 <= (1 - E(xi_tau)) E||e^{(k)}||^2 follows in three lines, with Hoeffding (Corollary Hoeffding-co) demoted to justifying Monte-Carlo estimation of E(xi_tau) via the stated sample complexity. This preserves the advertised rate 1 - E(xi_tau) (slightly improving it by removing epsilon) and the experimental methodology, but replaces the theorem's hypotheses and removes its stated high-probability concentration characterization.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem convRBSK_sharper's bound — the paper's flagship 'sharper' rate, advertised in the abstract ('With concentration inequalities, we derive new expected linear convergence rate bounds'), in the introduction and conclusions, and plotted as the 'Thm convRBSK_sharper bound' curves throughout Section sec:expResult — is unsupported by a valid proof.
issues.title: Theorem convRBSK_sharper: a high-probability sample-average inequality cannot be converted into the claimed deterministic expectation bound by 'taking expectation'
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained in a single theorem, uses the paper's own steps (no new global proof architecture), and leaves a recognizably comparable — in fact slightly stronger — expected-rate result; but it is a genuine reformulation of the statement and its hypotheses (population covariance instead of the sample-based high-probability formulation), which goes beyond a routine local fix. The stated theorem is not established as written.
